title: Array destructuring and swap patterns
hook: Array destructuring pulls elements by index in one line — swap two variables without a temp, skip entries with commas, and capture tails with rest.

blocks.text: **Array destructuring** `[a, b, ...rest] = arr` maps indices to bindings left-to-right. **Holes** skip positions: `[first, , third]`. **Defaults** apply when slot is **undefined** (empty slot or missing index). **Rest element** must be last — collects remaining indices into array. Works on **iterables** (not only Array) when used in for-of destructuring. **Swap**: `[a, b] = [b, a]` without temporary variable.

entries.plainDefinition: ...rest collects remaining items into new array.
Empty slot in pattern skips assigning that index.
Pattern works on any object with Symbol.iterator.

blocks.text: React `useState` returns `[state, setState]` — idiomatic array destructure. Parsing CSV rows, splitting RGB tuples, and algorithm interview swaps use this syntax. C# tuple deconstruction `(a, b) = (b, a)` is parallel. Sparse arrays and undefined slots confuse defaults — senior edge case.

blocks.title: Interview trap: rest must be last
blocks.body: const [...rest, last] = arr is SyntaxError. Only one rest per pattern, always final position.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Rest not last in pattern. Destructuring null/undefined iterable. Assuming length after destructure — rest may be empty. Using array destructure on object-returning API.

blocks.text: Prefer **object destructure** for named API returns when tuple order is unclear — `[data, error]` tuples need discipline. For perf-sensitive code, index access may beat destructure in tight loops. **Generators** destructure via iterator protocol — understand for advanced iterables.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Invalid rest placement. Cannot swap without temp using destructuring. Confusing array destructure with object destructure on {0: 'a'} object.

interviewTakeaways: Array destructure maps indices; comma skips slots.
Rest ... must be last; collects tail into new array.
[a,b]=[b,a] swaps without temporary — classic interview micro-task.
60s: Index-based unpack. Defaults for undefined slots. Rest last. Works on iterables. C# tuple (a,b) parallel. useState tuple idiom.
Follow-up: destructure first row from CSV string split.
commonPitfalls: Rest element not in final position — syntax error.
Using array pattern on function that returns object.
Strong answer: swap, holes, rest rules, sparse array defaults, tuple vs object return choice.
